references.phrase: ascending chain condition on a poset of ideals
references.context: Order theory: the ascending chain condition (ACC) on a partially ordered collection means each nondecreasing sequence x₁≤x₂≤⋯ is eventually constant. Here the collection is the ideals of R ordered by inclusion, and equality at intermediate steps is allowed.
references.reason: General ACC is a reusable order-theoretic stabilization property used for modules, ideals and arbitrary posets, independently of whether the particular ring is being called Noetherian.
references.matching_note: Compare prior candidate missing.8d9fdc1b1763aba61b63 (ascending chain of submodules) and generic Noetherian/maximal-element equivalences during global alias audit; do not silently equate the chain itself with its stabilization property.
